name: Street Custom 'Rat King' Cluster Munition Launcher
description: A improvised launcher cobbled from plumbing fixtures that fires a cluster of small explosive charges bound together with wire — typically six to ten individual charges that separate in flight and scatter across a 5-meter area upon a crude airburst fuse. Each sub-munition is roughly equivalent to a large firecracker in explosive yield, individually non-lethal but collectively capable of causing severe fragmentation injuries, starting fires, and creating enough chaos to cover a retreat or ambush. The Rat King pattern originated in Tier 1 gang warfare and has spread through fabrication networks.
specifications: sub-munitions: 6-10 per cluster launch range: 20-60 meters scatter radius: 5 meters individual charge yield: approximately 5g equivalent fragmentation: Wire binding and casing debris weight: 1.5-2.5 kg launcher, 0.8 kg per cluster reliability: Approximately 70% — duds and premature detonation are common
story_hooks: Rat King clusters have started appearing with military-grade sub-munitions instead of improvised charges — someone is feeding real ordnance into the street weapon supply chain.
A Tier 1 community has developed Rat King variants designed specifically to disable surveillance drones — they call it pest control.

physical_description.visual_profile: A brutalist pipe-and-steel contraption resembling a crude mortar or signal flare launcher. Oversized breach at the rear, tapered barrel of mismatched diameter tubing. The entire frame reads as industrial salvage held together by necessity rather than design—angular, unforgiving, built to fire once and worry about longevity later.
physical_description.dimensions: Launcher body: 58cm long, 12cm barrel diameter (irregular), 8cm wide at breech. Cluster munition: roughly spherical, 14cm diameter, 8cm height when bundled.
physical_description.weight_description: Hefty and front-heavy. The launcher alone feels like swinging a crowbar—2kg of dead mass that demands respect. Cluster rounds are dense, compact, deceptive in weight despite modest size. Favors two-handed shouldering.
physical_description.primary_material: Salvaged steel plumbing: Schedule 40 pipe, flanged couplings, brass fittings. Breech block welded from flat stock. Firing pin assembly is jury-rigged spring steel and hardened rod.
physical_description.finish: Industrial corrosion with deliberate preservation—unpainted bare steel showing orange rust bloom, intentionally retained for weight distribution and authentic DIY aesthetic. Welds are rough, visible, unskilled. Brass fittings retain dull tarnish.
physical_description.color_scheme: Dull rust-orange steel, aged brass, matte gunmetal grey on the firing mechanism. No paint, no finish—pure material honesty.
physical_description.grip_texture: Bare steel with shallow knurling marks from vice work. Cold to the touch. No ergonomic consideration—wrapped sections of frayed electrical tape at grip points where previous users' hands have worn the metal smooth.
distinctive_features: Misaligned barrel seams visible as dark stress lines
Hand-stamped serial numbers scratched into the breech: 'RK-7' or similar gang markers
Airburst fuse mechanism: crude brass pressure-release valve protruding from the side
Impact dimples and dents from field use and crude manufacturing
Rope-and-cleat aiming notch cut into the rear sight block
Residual black powder staining around the firing pin housing
Wire-wrapped cluster rounds nestled in a canvas sling, wires clearly visible
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: No corporate logo. Hand-scratched gang initials or fabricator tags stamped inside the barrel. Stamped 'STREET CUSTOM' in crude block letters on the breech flange, barely legible under rust.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-worn and well-used. Surface corrosion is active, not static. Firing pin shows bluing wear from repeated strikes. Evidence of jury-rigged repairs: re-welded stress points, replaced fittings. Residual powder burns and char marks around the muzzle and breech from dozens of fires. Looks dangerous because it is.
